form_gauss1827.apa: Gauss, C. F. (1902). General investigations of curved surfaces of 1827 and 1825 (J. C. Morehead & A. M. Hiltebeitel, Trans.). Princeton University Library. (Original work published 1827)

shots.caption: Art. 17: the element of any line on the surface, ds = √(E dp² + 2F dp dq + G dq²).
shots.quote: Let s be the length of such a curve, measured from an arbitrary initial point, and in either direction chosen as positive. Let θ denote the angle which the element ds = √(E dp² + 2F dp.dq + G dq²) makes with the line of the first system [formula read from the page image]
shots.why: The general line element, before Gauss's choice of coordinates.

shots.caption: Art. 19, p. 28: F = 0 for lines at right angles, E = 1 for p measured along shortest lines, √G = m; and at the common point, m = 0 and ∂m/∂p = 1.
shots.quote: orthogonally the lines of the second system; i. e., in such a way that we have generally ω = 90°, or F = 0. [...] it is evident that p and q denote now the same quantities that were expressed in Arts. 15, 16 by r and φ, and that E = 1. Thus the two preceding formulae become: [...] or, setting √G = m, k = −(1/m)·∂²m/∂p² [symbols read from the page image] [...] But in the particular case where all the lines p go out from the same point, evidently we must have m = 0 for p = 0. [...] we shall have for an infinitely small value of p, m = p, and consequently, for p = 0, m = 0 at the same time, and ∂m/∂p = 1.
shots.why: With E = 1, F = 0 and √G = m, the line element becomes ds² = dp² + m² dq².
